artworks.title: Dionysus and Oenopion
artworks.description: British Museum amphora B 210 shows Dionysus with Oenopion — the Chian king often named as the wine-god's son, who brought viticulture to Chios. Archaic vase-painting keeps the island's legendary wine-king beside his divine father.

artworks.title: Blind Orion Searching for the Rising Sun
artworks.description: Poussin's Met landscape shows the aftermath of Oenopion's revenge: Orion, blinded by the Chian king after assaulting Merope, rides toward the dawn that will restore his sight. The hunter's blindness is Oenopion's defining deed in the mythic cycle.

popCulture.title: Orion (mythology)
popCulture.description: The hunter's Chian episode makes Oenopion the king who blinds Orion for violating Merope — then hides in an underground (or iron) chamber when the giant returns for vengeance.

popCulture.title: Oenopion
popCulture.description: Legendary king of Chios, bringer of wine, son of Dionysus (or of Rhadamanthys and Ariadne) — remembered for the blinding of Orion.

popCulture.title: Chios
popCulture.description: Oenopion's island — assigned to him in Cretan tradition, famed for wine, and the stage of Orion's crime and punishment.
